ownerDecisions.decision: Q-MEMFD-5 (owner, via the lane monitor): "Scoped exception (Recommended)". Its scope: one file, src/harness_conformance/live_linux_boundary.py, and only three changes: the memfd flags (MFD_NOEXEC_SEAL), the coded refusal CREDENTIAL_MEMFD_NOEXEC_UNSUPPORTED on kernels without it, and the F_SEAL_EXEC assertion. It closes W01-AMEND QW3 = M-a. The record's ownerDecisions cite Q-MEMFD-5 and QW3.

W01-AMEND-QW3 (OWNER_DECIDED, as the snapshotted amendment states it): M-a, replacing a vm.memfd_noexec pin (which a CAP_SYS_ADMIN holder in the initial namespaces can lower): memfd_create flags become MFD_CLOEXEC | MFD_NOEXEC_SEAL, so the kernel clears exec and sets F_SEAL_EXEC on every call with no reliance on host state; carried by the W02d successor seccomp-allowlists-v2
